title: Pre-build AC decision is code, not prose (built, pending operator decision)
context: Eleven changes shipped without a written promise because the building agent chose the exemption by label.
decision: Code decides: whether anything observable changed is computed from the diff, AC text must read as an outcome (hard validation), the operator is asked only when an existing AC changes or goes away or no single FR owns a new AC, answers come only through a sha256-bound operator channel, the freeze is an append-only record compared with the catalog at finalize, and an unattended ask holds only its own unit. Unattended is derived from the loop environment or a campaign worktree; the operator-channel variable is a guard, not authentication, and every decision records answered_via.
consequences: No label, tier or keyword logic remains. An agent cannot assert an exemption or answer its own question. Built, pending operator decision: the brief's measure bar is not met and not measurable in this design (see the Q1 MEASURE file). The earlier lexical-HOW design replay is superseded.
rationale: Operator decision 2026-11-01: everything that code can decide is decided by code; AI only where code cannot decide.
rejected: A lexical HOW test as an ask trigger (false flags); hash-as-freeze (compare with the catalog instead); a wave-wide STRICT-STOP for a question; any label-based exemption
